result.title: Leveraging Segmentation Representations for Efficient Classification: A Self-Configuring Framework Based on nnU-Net
result.summary: We propose a self-configuring framework that extends the nnU-Net workflow to both segmentation and classification in 3D medical imaging. Building on nnU-Net's self-configuring method, the framework reuses representations learned by a segmentation model for image-level classification. Its encoder features and predicted segmentation probabilities are used by a lightweight classifier. Two information-sharing strategies are investigated. In the frozen-backbone branch, features are augmented with region-of-interest information, predicted foreground volume, and segmentation confidence. In the adaptation branch, the final encoder stage is partially fine-tuned for classification, with an auxiliary segmentation loss to preserve segmentation-related information. Additional five-fold experiments showed that more complex configurations did not consistently improve classification performance. On the public validation leaderboard, our selected framework achieved an Overall score of 0.8056. In the official FLARE 2026 Task 2 final evaluation, our framework ranked first overall, achieving the highest DSC, NSD, and AUROC across all four testing tasks, including two hidden testing tasks. Local inference measurements also remained below the challenge limits of $60 \mathrm{s}$ per case and $4 \mathrm{GB}$ GPU memory. These results demonstrate the practical value of reusing segmentation representations for classification while maintaining a simple and efficient framework.

AI.brief_summary: 该文基于 nnU-Net 构建自配置框架，把 3D 医学分割编码器特征与预测分割概率送入轻量分类器，比较「冻结骨干＋ROI、前景体积、分割置信度」与「末段部分微调＋辅助分割损失」两种信息共享策略，并在 FLARE 2026 Task 2 排名第一。
AI.relevance_reason: 把分割概率与置信度作为显式证据特征、并以辅助分割损失抑制信息流失，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据保留与内部状态被答案监督冲淡的问题提供可核查线索，但该工作属医学分割的下游分类应用，未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成与使用。
